verdict.rationale: OpenClaw is itself a personal AI assistant. Its docs describe chatting with it, delegating work through tools such as shell exec, browser control and computer use, and spawning background sub-agents for long tasks. A hands-on report confirms a user handed it multi-step home IT chores and got them done in a couple of hours. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of the end-to-end delegation workflow and its reliability limits (the evidence is mostly short doc snippets).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant for messaging, browser, desktop, and automation workflows.
Install OpenClaw, run onboarding, and chat with your AI assistant in about 5 minutes.
Parallelize research, long tasks, and slow tool work without blocking the main run.
A user handed OpenClaw home IT chores they had put off for years
